channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Expanding Anyma’s Coachella performance into broadcast AR with Unreal Engine
item.description: Anyma's Coachella show used Unreal Engine, MetaHuman and broadcast AR to bring its live-music visuals to a wide online audience.

item.title: Are the new wave of solo AI game-makers making any money? No, not really
item.description: Games built with AI tools like Claude Code are flooding the app stores, but very few are earning meaningful revenue or downloads — a sober look at solo AI game-making.

item.title: China's Game Market Revenue Hit 30 Billion Yuan in October, Down 4.27% YoY: Mobile Down 2.2%, PC Down 15%
item.description: Gamma Data reports China's game market revenue reached 30 billion yuan in October, down 4.27% year over year, with mobile down 2.2% and PC down 15%.

item.title: Creating Real-Time Desert Temple Environment In Unreal Engine 5
item.description: The author shares how he expanded a desert temple concept into a real-time scene, balancing realism and stylization.

item.title: Architecting a 60FPS Real-Time Multiplayer Stickman Battle Arena with HTML5 Canvas & WebSockets: The Engineering of Paper War
item.description: A hands-on breakdown of building a 60 FPS real-time multiplayer stickman battle arena in the browser with HTML5 Canvas and WebSockets, covering sync and game feel.

item.title: Gender Ratios Across 8 Popular Gacha Games: Genshin and Honkai: Star Rail Balanced, Wuthering Waves Leans Female
item.description: A data roundup of male-to-female character ratios across eight popular gacha games, and what each game's balance says about its audience.

item.title: What is a world boss event? A plain-English guide
item.description: A plain-English explainer of what world boss events are, how they work, and how one live game's event puts the pieces together.

item.title: Keep Unreal Engine 5 Projects Clean with This Optimization Toolkit
item.description: Leartes Studios' editor extension scores project health, finds unused assets and maps dependencies, helping Unreal Engine 5 developers keep their projects tidy.

item.title: Hacker Behind GTA 6 Leak Pleads Guilty to Rockstar Games Breach
item.description: The Lapsus$ member, previously ruled unfit to stand trial, admitted to the breach that leaked early GTA 6 footage and source code.

item.title: Exploring audio-driven facial performance for longer NPC dialogue
item.description: Longer NPC dialogue raises two production questions — how to generate convincing facial performance and keep it consistent across a scene — and this piece explores audio-driven approaches to both.

item.title: TexForge is out: a open-source image workbench for games and batch work
item.description: An MIT-licensed cross-platform desktop app that folds normal maps, channel packing, mipmap chains and 113 batch image actions into one workbench for Unity, Unreal, Godot and other engines.

item.title: Your sprite atlas validator may be checking data the JSON parser already changed
item.description: A sprite atlas can open and parse fine yet still be an ambiguous delivery — the gap hides between the JSON source text and the data your validator actually receives.

item.title: Report: South Korea's mobile game downloads fall 28% as revenue holds near $5bn
item.description: Sensor Tower's new report shows South Korean mobile game downloads fell from 540 million to 390 million over five years while in-app revenue held firm, as the market shifts from chasing downloads to retention and monetisation.

item.title: What the first 60 seconds of two idle browser games taught us (with real numbers)
item.description: Real numbers from two tiny 1.6 MB JavaScript idle games break down what keeps players past the first 60 seconds — practical data for web idle-game devs.

item.title: Unreal Insights in the Sprint: A Short Performance Pass You Can Finish Before Standup
item.description: A quick Unreal Insights performance pass you can finish before standup, turning profiling into a routine instead of a fire drill.

item.title: Hand Tracking vs Controllers in VR: How to Choose
item.description: Choose controllers when a VR game needs precision, buttons and haptic feedback, and hand tracking when ease of use matters more, such as training, casual play and public demos.

item.title: Designing a browser game older players can start in ten seconds: what the classics get right
item.description: Classic card, board and puzzle games need no tutorial, never punish slow reactions and allow undoing a mistake — design choices any browser game can borrow.

item.title: Godot Foundation welcomes Manus as Platinum Sponsor
item.description: Manus joins the Godot Foundation as a Platinum Sponsor, helping keep Godot free, open, and in constant development for everyone.

item.title: Wild Shift Devlog #6: I couldn't find my own @
item.description: The sixth devlog for Wild Shift, a GitHub Game Off 2026 entry, recounts a small readability bug — the player character @ kept vanishing into the grass — and the tweaks made so the hero stands out in a screen full of monochrome ASCII glyphs.

item.title: How BeamNG.drive Brought Its Soft-Body Physics to PS5
item.description: The BeamNG team shares how it kept the game's soft-body physics intact on PS5, and how it optimized memory and performance for the console.
